newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine banker says interest rates have to rise.
newsitem.headline: Philippine banker says interest rates have to rise.

text.p: Philippine interest rates should rise in order to curb the falling peso, Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP) president Rafael Buenaventura said on Friday.
"Interest rates will have to go up... I suspect it will," he said, when asked by reporters for his views on the weakening of the peso against the dollar.
The peso fell to as low as 26.345 against the dollar in early trading on Friday. It previously reached that level on Thursday, the lowest since October 1994.

The peso has been falling since the beginning of the week due to declining domestic interest rates which in turn came about because a cut in banks' reserve requirements triggered a flood of liquidity.
Analysts have blamed the narrowing interest rate differentials between the peso and the U.S. dollar as the cause for the heavy dollar buying.
"The moment that the differential has narrowed to a certain point, something has to give," Buenaventura said.
He said the Central Bank should start mopping up liquidity in the market, given that U.S. interest rates are bound to go up in the coming months due to the perceived strength of the economy.
"(The Central Bank) has to factor in the interest rate of the United States and the interest rates elsewhere because there are other alternative outlets (for investors)," he said.
"It's a tough balancing act," he added, when asked for his opinion on how high the local interest rates should be to stop the outflow of foreign exchange.
